Subject: Evidence rotation plan for UK IDTA + SCCs — subprocessor delegation timeline

Alex / Aurelia legal team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call, we're proposing a short, auditable "evidence rotation" approach for the UK IDTA + SCCs artifacts so your compliance team can sign off without a lengthy one-off handoff. High level: 

- What we will deliver by Dec 22: a packaged evidence bundle (see attachment) containing current policies, subprocessor attestations, sample access logs, and the subprocessor matrix.
- What we need from Aurelia by Jan 9: confirmation of which subprocessors (from the matrix) you require additional attestations for, and any specific retention extracts for sampled logs.
- Delegation ask: for cross-boundary subprocessors where Aurelia wants proof of control, we can issue a short-form delegation affidavit signed by Redwood and the subprocessor. That will be produced in the same bundle unless you prefer per-subprocessor issuance.

Open questions we raised that I wanted to put in writing:
1) Would you accept the bundle as the primary artifact with follow-up attestations on a 30-day cadence?
2) Any legal formatting constraints for handover (DocuSign vs. email-signed PDFs)?

Attachments: subprocessor_matrix_v2.xlsx (sheet: flagged_for_attest), uk-idta-evidence-pack.zip (placeholder: artifacts will be added).

I've cc'd Kimberly and Jonas from our transfer/evidence team — Kimberly will lead the packaging; Jonas will coordinate technical log slices if you need them.

Next steps: Alex, can you confirm (a) DocuSign acceptance and (b) whether there are two subprocessors you want prioritized for delegations?

Thanks,

--
Naomi Feldman
Privacy & Trust Programs
Redwood Inference

Naomi — thanks, this looks sensible. Couple quick notes from our side: 

- DocuSign is preferred for affidavits/attestations. We can accept an initial bundle via secure drive link but will need DocuSign for anything that is explicitly an "attestation".
- Priority subprocessors: MedTransit Ltd. and EdgeOps Inc. — our security team wants delegations for those two first.
- On the 30-day cadence: that's acceptable if each follow-up clearly lists any changed controls since the last bundle.

I'll loop in our legal counsel (cc'd) for any signature format comments. Can we get the first draft bundle by Dec 22 as you proposed? We have a procurement checkpoint on Jan 12 that depends on this.

Thanks — Alex

Thanks everyone — final confirmation and one operational tweak.

Confirmations: 
- Bundle delivery: Dec 22 (drive link) — will contain the artifacts Kimberly listed.
- DocuSign envelopes: Dec 20 for MedTransit Ltd. and EdgeOps Inc. attestations.
- 30-day rotation cadence accepted by Aurelia in-thread.

Operational tweak: instead of two separate envelopes for each subprocessor, we'll prepare a per-subprocessor combined envelope that includes (1) subprocessor affidavit, (2) Redwood's delegation statement, and (3) a brief control-change checklist to be re-signed on cadence. That reduces signature overhead and makes audit trails simpler.

Deliverables and owners: 
- Naomi: external comms and final bundle sign-off.
- Kimberly: artifact packaging and DocuSign orchestration.
- Jonas: technical log extraction and checksum manifests to prove tamper-evidence.

Alex — once you confirm acceptance of the combined-envelope idea and that Jan 12 procurement checkpoint is still the target, we'll proceed.
